{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjdzc8AAAABafZ9VA", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3IVzhEF0kQ", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3IV", "number": 69, "title": "Schedule SH-2 instruction fetch and decode ahead of execution on both CPUs", "body": "## Problem

Related to #17.

At main `7902b069c7fbcb612770a9254f3dc9b0c851381b`, `Cpu::execute` requests its opcode through `fetch16(pc)` immediately before execution. `CpuBus::fetch16` fetches an aligned longword and retains its companion halfword, but there is no independently scheduled IF/ID stream advancing alongside older instructions.

The existing load/store contracts explicitly limit precise overlap evidence to warmed instruction-cache execution. Cold and uncached instruction fetches consume retained overlap instead of participating in the complete pipeline schedule. This leaves a consequential CPU and shared-bus timing gap despite the successful load, store, multiplier and aligned-fetch increments.

## Expected outcome

Implement bounded, CPU-local instruction-fetch/decode scheduling for both SH-2s, integrated with the existing hardware clock, cache and transaction arbiter. Instruction availability and bus occupancy must arise from scheduled fetches rather than only adjusting an instruction's total cycle count.

The primary contract is the [Hitachi SH-1/SH-2 Programming Manual](https://antime.kapsi.fi/sega/files/h12p0.pdf), §§7.1–7.5, printed pp.168–176, especially Figures 7.1, 7.4 and 7.6–7.9. These establish overlapping stages, slot stretching and IF/MA contention. Applicable instruction diagrams in §7.7 determine control-flow transitions. Cross-check applicable corrections in the [Renesas Software Manual Rev.5.00](https://www.renesas.com/en/document/mah/sh-1sh-2sh-dsp-software-manual), §§7.1–7.4; exclude SH-DSP-only rules.

Use the [SH7604 Hardware Manual](https://antime.kapsi.fi/sega/files/sh7604.pdf), §§4.3–4.7, §6.3.2, §7.3.1, §7.11.2 and §8, for exception boundaries, UBC, external fetch geometry, write-buffer ordering and cache behavior.

Focused scope: instruction fetch/decode availability, its interaction with established execution/memory stages, and the redirects/cancellation needed to integrate it correctly. Preserve current instruction semantics and device contracts. Unrelated EX microsequences, A-bus read conversion, raster half-line timing and other chip improvements remain separate work. This does not require branch prediction.

## Context and reproduction

Inspect:

- `src/cpu.rs::Cpu::execute`, `src/cpu/timing.rs::LoadPipeline` and `MovAccess`.
- `src/bus.rs::CpuBus::fetch16`, cache/refill paths, and `src/bus/transactions.rs`.
- `src/lib.rs` processor-boundary scheduling.
- `docs/sh2-load-pipeline.md`, `docs/sh2-store-pipeline.md` and `docs/sh2-multiplier.md`.
- `src/bus/fetch_tests.rs`, existing load/store/multiplier scheduler vectors, and their native/browser guests.

Reproduce the missing scheduling with an independently authored stage trace: execute a straight-line stream containing register instructions and ordinary MOV accesses, varying instruction alignment, resident versus cold cache, P1 execution and programmed memory waits. Observe actual fetch requests/completions and instruction execution boundaries. The inherited implementation must fail at least one required scheduling oracle.

The supplied snapshot has no open task Issues. Recent validation records report passing native and browser regressions, but do not establish this missing behavior. No full suites were rerun during planning.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] Before changing production behavior, document a primary-derived IF/ID stage and cancellation table. Include cold entry, steady state, aligned longword/retained-halfword fetches, cache hit/miss/refill, P1, IF/MA contention and waited slots. Cite exact manual figures and applicable corrections. Separate hardware requirements from deterministic emulator conventions. Correct any mistaken AI-authored technical criteria in the source Issue with references and rationale; no human confirmation is required.

- [ ] Both CPUs schedule retained instruction bytes and decode readiness independently of architectural retirement. Literal native traces demonstrate fetch overlap with older non-memory stages, documented serialization against MA, and slot stretching under actual waits. Preserve existing MOV forwarding, dependency and multiplier interlocks without counting a contention interval twice.

- [ ] Exercise resident cache, cold misses, cache-line crossings, cache-disabled/P1 streams, both longword alignments and the fixed word-wide CS0 route. Preserve refill order, cache controls, software coherency, BSC waits and write-buffer read fencing. Fetches use real grants and sampled bytes; no instantaneous backing-memory reads or latency-only substitute may satisfy these checks.

- [ ] Native integration traces cover taken/untaken conditional branches, delayed branches/calls/returns and RTE, exception entry, IRQ/NMI deferral, UBC and SLEEP/wake. Redirected or discarded instructions cannot retire or alter architectural state. Preserve existing aligned-fetch/self-modification and address-error regressions unless an exact primary correction justifies a documented replacement. Do not invent undocumented speculative MMIO effects or convert discarded fetch activity into an unsupported architectural exception.

- [ ] Test pending and completed fetch work against peer CPU requests, on-chip DMAC, SCU DMA and refresh. Assert ownership, retained data, once-only effects and independent peer progress. Cover cancellation/restart through manual reset, cold/SYSRES, SSHOFF/SSHON and PLL changes using existing reset-domain contracts. Compare traces and results across advancement chunks 1/3/17/10000 and with passive inspection.

- [ ] Add a reproducible original MIT-licensed synthetic guest and manual-derived oracle. Both SH-2s execute cached and uncached/waited kernels, compute readback/arithmetic records, measure timing through guest FRT accesses and perform a shared-memory handoff. Include alignment, wait, operand and omitted-operation controls plus repeated cold boots. At least one unchanged oracle must fail on inherited main and pass after implementation; production traces must not generate expected values.

- [ ] Run the same guest bytes and authored expectations through rebuilt production Wasm in the required headless-browser suite under `/saturn-rust/`. Register fixture reproduction and browser coverage in the existing workflow. Preserve Star Collector, Prism Courier and Hardware Lab gameplay, graphics, sound, inputs, diagnostic computations and restart behavior. Any changed timing golden requires an independent stage derivation; do not relax substantive assertions to obtain green tests.

- [ ] Pass `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo build --locked`, `cargo test --locked`, native all-target Clippy and Wasm Clippy with `-D warnings`, `sh scripts/check-fixtures.sh`, `sh scripts/build-web.sh`, the complete existing `npm run test:browser`, applicable runner tests and whitespace checks. Record actual results and update architecture, conformance and validation documentation with precise implementation/test links and remaining deviations.

This is partial progress toward #17. Remaining CPU/peripheral semantics, complete bus/reset/arbitration, SCU/DSP, video/audio, CD/media/HLE, SMPC and comprehensive integration requirements remain mandatory. Leave #17's unmet scope open. Genuine BIOS and commercial-game compatibility remain unverified; passing this task cannot establish broad compatibility.

## Optional validation

Additional generated instruction-stream stress cases within the documented programming contract. No personal firmware, commercial discs, physical console, human approval or live Pages inspection is required.

## Required post-merge verification

None.
